trigger: Breach of unsecured PHI (presumed unless the 164.402 four-factor assessment shows low probability of compromise)
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery
notify: Each affected individual (first-class mail; substitute notice if 10+ have out-of-date contact information)

obligation: HIPAA breach notice to HHS (500 or more)
deadline: Contemporaneously with individual notice (within 60 days of discovery)
notify: HHS Secretary via the OCR breach portal

obligation: HIPAA breach log to HHS (fewer than 500)
deadline: Within 60 days after the end of the calendar year
notify: HHS Secretary via the OCR breach portal

trigger: Breach affecting more than 500 residents of a state or jurisdiction
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery
notify: Prominent media outlets serving that state or jurisdiction
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if more than 500 Florida residents

trigger: Law enforcement states notice would impede an investigation
deadline: Delay as specified in writing; up to 30 days if the statement is oral and documented

trigger: Breach of security of personal information (includes medical and health insurance information) of Florida residents
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach; HIPAA-compliant notice is deemed compliant if the practice timely provides a copy of that notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - confirm deemed-compliance path with counsel

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Attorney General)

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1000 individuals at one time
Affected patients who reside outside Florida
notify: Residents and regulators per each state's law

obligation: Business associate breach notice to the practice (inbound)
trigger: A business associate discovers a breach of the practice's PHI
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 days after discovery (BAAs may set shorter)

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
deadline: Before any payment; reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
Per policy (typically as soon as practicable; use the carrier's breach hotline before hiring vendors)

obligation: CIRCIA incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours; 24 hours after ransom payment
